new_entities.name: PQQ mitochondrial supplement
new_entities.description: Dietary supplementation with pyrroloquinoline quinone, typically marketed for mitochondrial, cognitive, or energy support.

new_entities.name: Human outcomes
new_entities.description: Overall clinically meaningful outcomes reported in human use, including benefit, harm, or lack of validated efficacy.

edges.effect_quant: A small 41-person placebo-controlled trial reported modest improvements on selected attention and visual-spatial tasks after 12 weeks of BioPQQ, but a later glaucoma crossover trial tested PQQ only as part of a multi-ingredient combination, making attribution impossible. Human evidence therefore remains exploratory rather than definitive.
edges.population: adults taking oral PQQ supplements for cognition, mitochondrial support, or general wellness goals
edges.mechanism: PQQ is promoted as a redox-active cofactor that may support mitochondrial biogenesis and oxidative-stress responses, but mechanistic plausibility still exceeds demonstrated human clinical benefit.
edges.summary: This is a low-certainty supplement edge. There are early positive human signals, but the literature is sparse, underpowered, and often confounded by combination products or mechanistic overinterpretation.
edges.caveats: Do not market PQQ as a proven mitochondrial therapy. Most of the enthusiasm still comes from preclinical biology and small human experiments rather than replicated clinical outcome trials.

evidence.citation: Nakano M et al 2016 Adv Exp Med Biol
evidence.notes: Effect of the Antioxidant Supplement Pyrroloquinoline Quinone Disodium Salt (BioPQQ™) on Cognitive Functions.
